name: Guesty
tagline: Property management platform for short-term rental hosts and managers: channel sync, unified guest inbox, automation, payments and reporting.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Guesty quotes per listing and tier, often with a booking-revenue component.

verdictSummary: Guesty's actual product is not the dashboard, it is certified two-way connectivity to Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo and friends, plus payments and the messaging pipes on top. Those APIs are gated behind partner programs with onboarding, certification and volume expectations, so a personal build cannot legally or practically push rates, accept reservations or reply to guest messages inside the channels. What you can build in a weekend is the read-only half: pull the public iCal feeds every listing exposes, merge them into one calendar, catch overlaps before they become double bookings, and generate cleaning tasks and payout statements. That covers the anxiety of a two-listing host quite well and covers almost nothing of a hundred-listing manager. The moment you need rate parity, unified inbox or automatic guest charging, you are back to a platform with signed channel agreements.
coreLoopDIY: Pulls every listing's public iCal feed on a schedule into a local SQLite database, shows one merged calendar, flags overlapping or suspicious bookings, and turns each stay into cleaning tasks and a simple monthly payout sheet.
requirements: iCal export URLs for each listing from Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com or your direct booking tool
Node 20 plus local disk for SQLite
A machine or small VPS that can run a scheduled refresh every 15 to 60 minutes
Manual entry of nightly rates and payouts, since iCal carries no money data
whatYouLose: Two-way channel sync: no rate, availability or minimum-stay push, so overbooking prevention is reactive instead of blocking
Unified guest inbox and automated messaging, including the templated check-in and review nudges that actually drive ratings
Payment processing, deposits, damage protection and multi-currency payouts
Dynamic pricing, market comps and occupancy benchmarking built from cross-portfolio data
Owner portals, accounting exports, task assignment for cleaning crews, and someone to call when a channel API changes overnight
moatNotes: Airbnb and Booking.com connectivity is a partner program, not a public API key. That gate is the whole business.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a double booking on Airbnb costs money, a penalty and a ranking hit, and the only way to prevent it reliably is to be the system of record that pushes availability to every channel in real time. Guesty holds the certified connections, the payment rails and the guest messaging history, and it absorbs the maintenance when a channel changes its API. For a single host with two listings that is arguably overkill, and iCal plus discipline gets you most of the way. For anyone managing other people's properties, the platform is also the audit trail, the owner statement and the liability shield, which no local script provides.
notes: The calendar merge is a weekend project; the channel connections are not. The moat is certified two-way connectivity to Airbnb and Booking.com, which you cannot buy with an API key.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user short-term rental calendar aggregator called "hostdesk". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: TypeScript, Next.js App Router, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM, Tailwind. Everything runs with `npm run dev` on localhost. Data lives in ./data/hostdesk.db.

What it does:
1. Listings table: name, nickname, address, default cleaning fee, notes.
2. Each listing has one or more iCal feed URLs (Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, direct). Feeds are stored in the database, not .env, and are editable in the UI.
3. A refresh job fetches every feed, parses VEVENTs with node-ical, and upserts reservations keyed by UID plus feed id. Keep a history row so changed or cancelled events are visible instead of silently vanishing.
4. Conflict detection: any two reservations for the same listing whose date ranges overlap get flagged loudly on a dashboard. Also flag same-day turnovers and stays that appear on one feed but disappeared from it on the next pull.
5. Unified calendar view: month grid, one row per listing, color per source channel. Click a block to see raw iCal fields.
6. Turnover list: for every checkout, auto-create a cleaning task with due date and a done checkbox. Simple list view, filterable by listing and week.
7. Money, manual only: let me enter gross payout per reservation and see a monthly per-listing summary of nights booked, occupancy percent, gross, cleaning fees and net. No integrations, no scraping of payout pages.
8. Refresh runs on an interval via a small node script (npm run refresh) plus a "Refresh now" button. Log each run with timestamp, feeds fetched and errors.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: writing to any channel, pushing rates or availability, guest messaging, payment processing, Airbnb or Booking.com partner APIs, scraping logged-in pages, multi-user roles, mobile apps.

Secrets: none needed, but read any optional basic-auth password from .env and gitignore ./data.

Deliver a README that states plainly where to find each channel's iCal export URL and warns that iCal sync is read-only and lags by up to a few hours, so this prevents surprises, it does not prevent double bookings.
